snapshot.title: CVE-2026-73309: XenForo before 2.3.13 contains an authentication bypass vulnerability in the OAuth2 token endpoint that allows unauthenticated attackers to obtain valid token pairs by submitting empty values for client_secret and code_verifier parameters.  / CVE-2026-73309: Empty OAuth2 credentials bypass
snapshot.digest:
XenForo before 2.3.13 contains an authentication bypass vulnerability in the OAuth2 token endpoint that allows unauthenticated attackers to obtain valid token pairs by submitting empty values for client_secret and code_verifier parameters. Attackers can exploit PHP truthy evaluation logic, which treats empty strings as false and skips client secret validation and PKCE code verifier validation, to exchange a valid authorization code for a token pair without proving client identity or holding the PKCE commitment.

BACK .WEB.OAUTH XenForo / OAuth2 08 Sept 2026 · 3 min POST VIEW TEXT / UTF-8 ADDRESS MARKDOWN BYTES XenForo 2.3.12 build 2031270 accepted empty OAuth2 credentials at the token endpoint. An empty PKCE verifier allowed an authorization code to be redeemed without proving possession of the original verifier. Empty client secrets affected authorization-code and refresh-token grants through the same code pattern. Technical details The token endpoint called assertRequiredApiInput() , which checked that the parameter existed but did not require a non-empty value. Credential verification was then guarded by truthiness checks: if ($input[ 'client_secret' ]) { /* compare it */ } if ($input[ 'code_verifier' ]) { /* verify PKCE */ } PHP evaluates both '' and '0' as false, so either value bypassed the comparison block. Reproduction Complete a normal S256 authorization flow for a public OAuth2 client and capture the authorization code. Exchange the code at the token endpoint with code_verifier= instead of the verifier used to create the challenge. Use the returned access token to request /api/me . The server returned access and refresh tokens, and /api/me accepted the access token. Supplying an incorrect non-empty verifier caused the exchange to fail. Impact Anyone who obtained a live authorization code for a public client could redeem it without the PKCE verifier. The issued tokens retained the user-approved scopes. Exploitation still required a valid authorization code. XenForo 2.3.13 rejects empty credentials before processing the grant. References CVE-2026-73309 PoC VulnCheck advisory XenForo 2.3.13 release 1888 UTF-8 BYTES .WEB.OAUTH · ADDRESSES ARE UTF-8 BYTE OFFSETS

snapshot.title: CVE-2026-73310: XenForo before 2.3.13 contains an authorization flaw in the OAuth2 token endpoint that allows attackers controlling any allowlisted redirect URI to bypass redirect URI binding by submitting a different allowlisted URI than the one recorded  / CVE-2026-73310: OAuth2 redirect URI mismatch
snapshot.digest:
XenForo before 2.3.13 contains an authorization flaw in the OAuth2 token endpoint that allows attackers controlling any allowlisted redirect URI to bypass redirect URI binding by submitting a different allowlisted URI than the one recorded at authorization time. Attackers can exchange an intercepted authorization code using a mismatched redirect URI to steal OAuth2 tokens from intercepted authorization flows.

BACK .WEB.OAUTH XenForo / OAuth2 08 Sept 2026 · 3 min POST VIEW TEXT / UTF-8 ADDRESS MARKDOWN BYTES XenForo 2.3.12 build 2031270 did not bind an OAuth2 authorization code to the redirect URI used during authorization. A code issued for one registered callback could be redeemed through another callback registered to the same client. Technical details XenForo stored the selected redirect URI on the OAuthRequest . During token redemption, the server only checked whether the submitted redirect_uri appeared in the client’s allowlist. It did not compare that value with the URI attached to the authorization request that issued the code. Reproduction Register callback A and callback B on the same client. Authorize with callback A. Exchange the resulting code while sending callback B. Use the returned token at /api/me . The token endpoint returned an access token, and the token authenticated as the user who authorized through callback A. Impact An attacker with a valid authorization code and control of another registered callback could redeem the code through that callback. Relevant cases include abandoned endpoints and custom URI schemes claimed by another application. The attack does not bypass the requirement for a valid code. XenForo 2.3.13 binds the submitted redirect URI to the authorization request that produced the code. References CVE-2026-73310 PoC VulnCheck advisory XenForo 2.3.13 release 1679 UTF-8 BYTES .WEB.OAUTH · ADDRESSES ARE UTF-8 BYTE OFFSETS

snapshot.title: CVE-2026-73311: XenForo before 2.3.13 contains an OAuth2 authorization code reuse vulnerability that allows attackers to obtain unauthorized token pairs by submitting a previously used authorization code. Attackers can exploit the failure to invalidate or  / CVE-2026-73311: OAuth2 authorization code replay
snapshot.digest:
XenForo before 2.3.13 contains an OAuth2 authorization code reuse vulnerability that allows attackers to obtain unauthorized token pairs by submitting a previously used authorization code. Attackers can exploit the failure to invalidate or mark authorization codes as consumed after initial token issuance to receive an independent token pair for the same user and scopes, bypassing the single-use guarantee of the OAuth2 authorization code flow.

BACK .WEB.OAUTH XenForo / OAuth2 08 Sept 2026 · 3 min POST VIEW TEXT / UTF-8 ADDRESS MARKDOWN BYTES XenForo 2.3.12 build 2031270 allowed the same OAuth2 authorization code to be redeemed more than once. Each successful exchange created a separate access token and refresh-token family. Technical details grantAuthorizationCode() loaded the code, checked isValid() and created the tokens. It then returned the response without deleting the code or marking it as used. Two simultaneous requests could also pass the validity check before either one finished. Reproduction Complete an OAuth2 authorization flow and capture the token request. Send the request once and record the returned access and refresh tokens. Send the same request again with the same authorization code. Verify both access tokens at /api/me . Both exchanges returned HTTP 200. The responses contained different access tokens and different refresh tokens for the same user. Impact Anyone able to capture a complete valid token request could replay it until the authorization code expired. Client authentication and PKCE material remained required where applicable. Every replay created another refresh-token family. XenForo 2.3.13 consumes the authorization code while issuing tokens, including for concurrent exchanges. snapshot.title: CVE-2026-73312: XenForo before 2.3.13 contains a refresh token replay vulnerability that allows attackers to reuse a refresh token multiple times by exploiting the failure to mark tokens as consumed when the parent access token has expired. Attackers can r / CVE-2026-73312: Refresh token replay after access-token expiry
snapshot.digest:
XenForo before 2.3.13 contains a refresh token replay vulnerability that allows attackers to reuse a refresh token multiple times by exploiting the failure to mark tokens as consumed when the parent access token has expired. Attackers can repeatedly submit the same refresh token to generate additional independent token pairs, achieving persistent unauthorized access for the token's full lifetime.

BACK .WEB.OAUTH XenForo / OAuth2 08 Sept 2026 · 3 min POST VIEW TEXT / UTF-8 ADDRESS MARKDOWN BYTES XenForo 2.3.12 build 2031270 allowed a refresh token to be reused after its associated access token expired. Each replay issued a new access-token and refresh-token pair with the same user and scopes. Technical details The refresh endpoint created the replacement pair and then called the old access token’s revocation routine. That routine started by checking whether the access token was still valid. An expired token failed immediately, so the function returned before revoking anything—including the related refresh token. Reproduction Obtain a valid OAuth2 access token and its refresh token. Wait for the access token to expire. Submit the refresh token and record the replacement pair. Submit the original refresh token again. Verify both returned access tokens at /api/me . Both refresh requests succeeded, and the original refresh token remained usable. Impact Anyone holding the refresh token could continue creating valid token pairs after the parent access token expired. Confidential clients still required their client secret. XenForo 2.3.13 consumes the refresh token independently of its expired parent and issues the replacement in the same operation. snapshot.title: CVE-2026-66635: Unauthenticated Cross Site Request Forgery (CSRF) in Slider by 10Web <= 1.2.62 versions. / CVE-2026-15993: The Form Maker by 10Web – Mobile-Friendly Drag & Drop Contact Form Builder plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to blind SQL Injection via '{username}' Placeholder in Dynamic-Choice Field WHERE Clause in all versions up to, and including, 1.1
snapshot.digest:
Unauthenticated Cross Site Request Forgery (CSRF) in Slider by 10Web <= 1.2.62 versions.

The Form Maker by 10Web – Mobile-Friendly Drag & Drop Contact Form Builder plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to blind SQL Injection via '{username}' Placeholder in Dynamic-Choice Field WHERE Clause in all versions up to, and including, 1.15.44 due to insufficient escaping on the user supplied parameter and lack of sufficient preparation on the existing SQL query. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with subscriber-level access and above, to append additional SQL queries into already existing queries that can be used to extract sensitive information from the database.
